title: Navigate from an authorized Command Incident to its visible Case Queue projection
goal: Expose the current single, independently authorized Command Incident projection as an exact Case Queue filter and preserve it across paged Case Workspace navigation/return; do not implement a Command relation service.
invariants: An Incident filter matches only the exact opaque identity of a Command Incident projection independently authorized for the selected current Case; a case with an unauthorized/missing Incident projection is not a match.
Current first-party Queue Saved View, sorted filtering, pagination, selected-page handoff and return tokens remain one engine, with independent authorization on all requests.
Incident IDs are opaque identifiers and must not be trimmed, case-folded, used to establish tenant/environment or treated as authorization.
This bounds to the currently projected single IncidentContext; no assertion that all canonical Case linked-incidents are enumerated, no Command relation provider or mutation.
security_properties: Every returned Case and linked Incident must pass the original server-side Case and Incident object-read checks, including after ACL changes.
Missing, cross-tenant or access-denied Incident context cannot disclose its identity via source matching, list, counts or return state.
Malformed/duplicate/unknown query controls fail before the session provider; the untrusted incident_id selects neither scope nor permissions.

migration.rationale: Optional HTTP filter reusing read-only first-party projection, no durable schema change.

rollback.strategy: Remove opt-in incident_id filter; old Queue, page and Workspace open/return remain available.

inputs: CAP-INV-101 section 17: Command Incident -> related Cases in Queue or Workspace.
Existing first-party Queue projection supports current independently authorized single optional IncidentContext but native HTTP cannot constrain Cases to a selected Incident ID.
Parent PR #145 frozen HEAD d31c326a785134e06b86fa79c9d8701d0a287a27, engineering-kernel run 39305417608 SUCCESS; PR and upstream draft, L2 report not verified.
outputs: Optional GET /case-queue?incident_id=opaque returns only Case rows whose independently authorized visible IncidentContext has exactly that opaque ID.
The existing Queue page cursor, Workspace handoff and POST return preserve and re-authorize selected Incident-linked filter as presentation only.
Same behavior with host-owned Shared Saved View selection when supplied, without new Command relationship engine.
acceptance_tests: Real Go httptest with multiple Cases, incident owner ACL separately allow/deny and Case ACL allow/deny: only Cases with exact linked Incident IDs visible, no denied metadata and no casefold ID alias.

Native incident-filtered pagination then Case Workspace open and POST return restore exact incident_id selector, sort, cursor, scroll and selection; revocation of incident rights refuses stale return.
Strict query duplicate/injected controls rejected before owner/session; original Queue HTTP tests, saved views, paging, security checks remain green.

performance_budget.rationale: One existing <=5000 owner candidate authorization and first-party projection, no new traversal or query engine.
metrics: no additional full projection pass beyond existing handoff/paging
